newsitem.title: USA: Italy to meet Emu criteria in 1997 -- Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italy to meet Emu criteria in 1997 -- Ciampi.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi repeated his confidence that Italy will meet the 3 percent deficit/GDP ratio required to join European economic and monetary union in 1997.

Italy would also meet the other requirements, except the debt requirement, he said in a speech prepared for delivery at the IMF Interim Committee. He added that such progress will be made sustainable by adopting permanent measures to replace some one-off provisions.

Ciampi also said that the government will now review the current social security system to verify whether the pace of adjustment introduced by the previous reforms needs to be quickened to ensure better medium-term sustainability.

"We are confident that by the end of 1997 we will have reached all the Maastricht targets, except for the debt-to-GDP ratio" Ciampi says, recalling the lira's re-entry in the exchang rate mechanism late last year, and the drop in inflation.
"Interest rates went down, more than in other European countries. They are expected to be comfortably in the acceptable range."

"The measures taken, together with the expected decline in interest expenditures, are quantitatively sufficient to meet the deficit target for 1997. Qualitatively, they can and will be improved with the 1998 Budget Law. We plan to rebalance the one-off measures taken in 1997 with permanent ones".
Ciampi added that the privatisation process has met all its main 1996 targets and will continue with renewed strength in 1997.

"Markets have understood and given credence to the multi-faceted adjustment strategy we are following. Interest rate differentials on government bonds have declined dramatically (from 1995 peaks) ... This should facilitate the task of reducing the budget deficit in the course of the current year," he said.

All this will produce benefits on the productive system Ciampi said, affirming that lower inflation and continued fiscal consolidation "should create the conditions for further reductions in interest rates and shift resources from the public to the private sector.

Noting that the economic upturn in Europe should help the business cycle, Ciampi says he expects "an appreciable recovery of the Italian economy in the course of 1997, of which signs are already visible, and a further acceleration of growth into 1998."
Turning to Europe, he said he saw encouraging signs of recovery while the process of disinflation and fiscal adjustments undertaken by many European couontries is now "in the final stretch."
"It must be completed. After that we must ensure that it can continue," he added.
